summary:
Our project is an educational, story driven exploration game named "I Need Space". 

The game follows an astronaut sent to investigate a mysterious signal originating from forgotten space missions. Through exploration of the Moon and Mars, players discover abandoned NASA equipment.

Rather than simply presenting historical information, the game allows players to interact with these machines, examine their components, and unlock archives explaining their engineering, scientific purposes, and contributions to space exploration.
details:
1. What does it do and how does it work?

"I Need Space" is an interactive, browser-based educational narrative game where players investigate a mysterious signal originating from the Moon and Mars. As players traverse lunar regolith and Martian terrain, they discover discarded and forgotten NASA equipment. The core gameplay revolves around scanning these artifacts to unlock deep, interactive archives that reveal their real-world engineering, scientific purpose, and mission history.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Low Barrier to Access: Built entirely for web browsers, removing installation hurdles and making it instantly playable across desktop and mobile devices.
  • Active Learning: Transforms dry historical facts and technical documentation into an immersive archaeological mystery, turning passive reading into active discovery.
  • Narrative Immersion: Blends atmospheric storytelling with hard science, keeping players emotionally and intellectually invested.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

The project aims to raise public awareness about forgotten space missions, spotlighting the uncelebrated milestones and hardware left behind during humanity's early push into the cosmos. It bridges STEM education and gaming, inspiring younger audiences to appreciate aerospace engineering, planetary science, and the legacy of space exploration.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you develop with?

  • Languages: HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript for robust, cross-platform browser compatibility and responsive UI handling.
  • Design & Asset Workflow: Figma for interface layouts and UI/UX wireframing; Canva and digital asset tools for polishing visual layouts.
  • Data Sources: Official NASA mission datasets, archives, and historical documentation regarding discarded lunar and Martian equipment.

5. How is your project creative?

It uniquely fuses science fiction mystery with authentic historical education. Rather than a standard shoot-em-up or generic sci-fi simulator, the gameplay focuses on cosmic archaeology—treating real engineering feats as rare collectibles. It also uses a nostalgic, vintage visual novel aesthetic that sets it apart from hyper-modern or overtly flashy tech demos.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Scientific Accuracy: Ensuring that the lore, equipment mechanics, and mission histories align closely with real NASA archives.
  • Educational Value vs. Fun: Balancing deep informational logs with snappy, engaging game pacing so players never feel like they are reading a textbook.
  • Accessibility & Performance: Optimizing lightweight web technologies so the game loads quickly and runs smoothly on lower-end devices or mobile browsers.
